label: rejected

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter, silhouette and top all read immediately as a single flower: a bloom on a stem with two leaves.
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: bloom disc (big), two leaves (medium), gold centre and petal tips (small).
evidence.V3: Stiff, perfectly straight prism stem of constant thickness and flat paper-card leaves read as primitives. Only the bloom is stylised.
evidence.V4: Petals are hard-faceted wedges with sharp ridges, the leaves are razor-thin cards, and the stem has hard prism corners, so edge treatment is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close bloom studio shows strong flat faceting on every petal, and the leaves close-up shows hard prism edges down the stem. These are minor stray facets on an organic form.
evidence.V6: Petal hue in 2-3 values, leaf-green secondary in 2 values and a gold centre accent. Disciplined, and the colourways (bluebell, sunset) swap only the petal hue.
evidence.V7: 388 tris against a small target of 600, so it is under target.
evidence.V8: Correct single vertex-colour material and kit palette, but the faceted, gem-like petals and prism stem do not match the kit's fused, smooth-shaded organic shells.
evidence.V9: Studio line: foliage, no collision/touch/query, Box fidelity, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre. Correct.

artifacts: faceted petal surfaces with hard ridges
top_fixes: Smooth-shade the petals (weighted normals, a rounded cupped petal profile) instead of gem-like facets
Taper and slightly curve the stem and give it a round cross-section
Give the leaves a slight fold/curl and thickness at the base so they read less like paper cards
